summary: The model could not identify the plant or disease with sufficient diagnostic certainty. No treatment should be administered blindly.

organic_measures.name: General Field Hygiene
organic_measures.method: Inspect adjacent plants for similar symptoms. Prune any visibly rotten or dead plant material using sterilized tools.

organic_measures.name: Neem Oil / Botanical Repellent (Preventive only)
organic_measures.method: If general sucking insect pests are visible, a mild spray of cold-pressed neem oil (3-5 ml per liter with mild soap) can act as a broad deterrent.
organic_measures.application: Foliar spray during low-sunlight hours (early morning or late evening)

prevention_measures: Capture a clear, well-focused close-up photo of the affected plant part in natural daylight.
Ensure the photo shows both healthy and symptomatic leaf or stem areas without severe shadows, blur, or glare.
Avoid applying broad-spectrum synthetic chemical pesticides without a verified diagnostic confirmation.
Take fresh physical plant samples to your nearest agricultural university, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), or certified crop consultant.
photo_guidance: Ensure good natural daylight (avoid direct harsh midday sun or deep shadows).
Focus sharply on the lesion or affected area.
Include both the top surface and underside of the leaf if possible.
Avoid taking photos with messy backgrounds, hands covering symptoms, or heavy motion blur.
sources: UC Davis IPM Plant Health Diagnostic Series
